raw_case_text: A 73-year-old woman with past medical history of hypertension and rheumatoid arthritis stage 4 under regular anti-hypertension medication and long-term corticosteroid therapy, presented to us in August 2010 with the chief complaint of decline of visual acuity of her right eye and right periorbital pain for 2 months. At the beginning of the clinical course, she had brain computed tomography (CT) scan and orbit magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) done in June 2010, which disclosed a small enhancing lesion, about 1.2 cm x 1.1 cm x 1 cm in size, near the right side orbital apex and adjacent right side superior orbital fissure with mild encasement of the right optic nerve, and this lesion showed mild extension to the adjacent right side posterior ethmoid sinus [Figure 1 a, b]. She had pulse steroid therapy in ophthalmology service, but it was ineffective. On admission, her neurological examination showed that she had right eye blindness, right ptosis, right ophthmaloplegia, and tingle in the territory of ophthalmic branch of right trigeminal nerve. Repeated MRI of orbit after admission in August 2010 showed the progression of the lesion which enlarged up to 1.5 cm x 1.3 cm x 1.2 cm [Figure 2 a, b]. She underwent endoscopic endonasal transethmoid approach with the removal of the lesion on 19 August 2010 under general anesthesia. After the surgery, she recovered well and her right periorbital pain was much released. However, 5 days after surgery, she experienced a severe headache followed by loss of consciousness. After endotracheal tube intubation and resuscitation, brain CT was checked which showed diffuse high-density acute SAH in the basal cistern, pre-pontine cistern, ambient cistern, quadrigeminal cistern, cerebellomedullary cistern, and right sylvian fissure, with acute hydrocephalus [Figure 3a]. Emergent external ventricular drainage was done followed by performing CT angiography which showed several bleb-like wide base aneurysms over right supraclinoid internal carotid artery (ICA), and one aneurysm, about 4 mm in size and located at the medial side of the right supraclinoid internal carotid artery, showed extravasation of contrast medium. The dome of the ruptured aneurysm projected medially and superiorly [Figure 3b]. On the same day, the histology examination reported that the lesion was composed of many fungal septate hyphae demonstrated on both HE stain and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain [Figure 4a, b]. Fungal infection was diagnosed and the culture turned out to be Aspergillus fumigatus. Her intracranial aneurysms were probably fungal aneurysms, which are one of the sequels of central nervous system (CNS) fungal infection. Unfortunately, after the event, she remained in deep coma and finally she expired due to central failure.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 73-year-old woman on long-term corticosteroids for rheumatoid arthritis presented with a 2-month history of progressive right-sided visual loss and right periorbital pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In June 2010, the patient developed right periorbital pain and declining right visual acuity. Initial brain CT and orbital MRI revealed a 1.2 x 1.1 x 1.0 cm enhancing right orbital apex lesion extending into the superior orbital fissure and right posterior ethmoid sinus; she received pulse corticosteroid therapy in an ophthalmology clinic without improvement, and her vision deteriorated to complete right eye blindness with ptosis and ophthalmoplegia by the time of admission in August 2010.
subjective.past_medical_history: Stage 4 rheumatoid arthritis on long-term corticosteroid therapy; hypertension on regular antihypertensive medication.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right eye blindness, right periorbital pain, right ptosis, diplopia/ophthalmoplegia, and right V1 trigeminal paresthesia; 5 days postoperatively developed sudden severe headache and coma.

objective.physical_examination: Admission neurological and ophthalmic examination revealed complete blindness of the right eye, right upper eyelid ptosis, total right ophthalmoplegia, and tingling paresthesia in the ophthalmic division (V1) of the right trigeminal nerve. Five days postoperatively, she developed deep coma.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial orbital MRI (June 2010) showed a 1.2 x 1.1 x 1.0 cm enhancing mass at the right orbital apex and superior orbital fissure mildly encasing the right optic nerve and extending to the right posterior ethmoid sinus; repeat orbital MRI on admission (August 2010) showed enlargement to 1.5 x 1.3 x 1.2 cm. She underwent endoscopic endonasal transethmoid resection on August 19, 2010; histopathology (H&E and PAS stains) revealed abundant septate fungal hyphae and tissue culture grew Aspergillus fumigatus. Five days postoperatively, emergent head CT for sudden headache and coma demonstrated diffuse acute subarachnoid hemorrhage across the basal, prepontine, ambient, quadrigeminal, and cerebellomedullary cisterns and right Sylvian fissure with acute hydrocephalus, and CT angiography revealed multiple bleb-like wide-based mycotic aneurysms of the right supraclinoid internal carotid artery (ICA), including a ruptured 4-mm medial supraclinoid ICA aneurysm with active contrast extravasation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Right orbital apex and posterior ethmoid invasive aspergillosis (Aspergillus fumigatus) complicated by fatal rupture of right supraclinoid internal carotid artery mycotic aneurysms causing diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage and acute hydrocephalus, confirmed by endoscopic biopsy histopathology (H&E and PAS stains), fungal culture growing A. fumigatus, and cerebral CT angiography. Despite initial pain relief after endoscopic endonasal transethmoid resection and emergent external ventricular drainage following aneurysmal rupture on postoperative day 5, the patient remained in a deep coma and died of central brain failure.
